in_hebrew.name: הליסיה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם הליסיה נגזר מהמילים העבריות 'אל' ו-'ישוע', שפירושן 'אלוהים הוא ישועתי'. השם מבטא את האמונה באלוהים כמושיע ומחסה.

in_greek.name: Ἠλισία
in_greek.meaning: Ἠλισία - ὁ Θεός ἡ σωτηρία μου
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ Ἠλισία ὄνομα προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὶς ἑβραϊκὲς λέξεις 'אל' καὶ 'ישוע', ὅπου σημαίνει ὁ Θεὸς ἡ σωτηρία μου. Ἐκφράζει τὴν πίστη εἰς τὸν Θεὸν ὡς Σωτήρα καὶ Προστατευτή.

in_latin.name: Helisia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Helisia derivatur ex vocibus hebraicis 'אל' et 'ישוע', quae significant 'Deus est salus mea'. Nomen hoc exprimit fidem in Deum ut Salvatorem et Refugium.

in_english.name: Helisia

historical_references.reference: Helisia, daughter of King Heli, was the mother of John the Baptist according to the New Testament. This Helisia is mentioned in the Gospel of Luke (1:5-7). Heli was a priest descended from Aaron (Luke 1:5), and his wife was named Elisheba. Helisia and Heli lived in the town of Gilgal during the reign of King Herod the Great (37-4 BC).

historical_references.reference: Helisia, also known as Helena of Constantinople, was a Christian saint and the wife of Constantius III, Roman Emperor from 421-425 AD. She is venerated as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches. Helisia is particularly remembered for her efforts to recover the True Cross of Jesus Christ. According to legend, she discovered the cross in Jerusalem and returned it to Constantinople in a great procession.
